The presence of compound literals, such as `sizeof(int){0}`, adds complexity by requiring additional backtracking, while also allowing for postfix operators like `sizeof(T){}.x[0]()`. A more effective solution involves expanding the special case for compound literals and writing a function that attempts to parse either unary expressions or parenthesized type names without backtracking.
